text:
michael: Hey @people-ops — quick heads up. I just saw my doc about early-stage RSI in my wrists. I need to reduce heavy typing for ~6 weeks and want to request an accommodation to shift more toward code review/docs and fewer PRs that require long typing sessions.

anya: Sorry to hear that, Michael. We can help. Can you DM a brief doctor's note or upload to the HR portal? We treat this confidentially. Also can you give an estimated start date?

michael: I can upload the note today. Start date would be Monday. Prefer details stay private — only on a need-to-know basis.

jamie: Thanks for flagging, @michael — I support this and we can reassign some tickets. We'll need a coverage plan for on-call and urgent bugs. Happy to redistribute work to keep you productive.

anya: We'll initiate the ADA interactive process — that means we document limitations and discuss reasonable adjustments. Typical temporary options: reduced typing, pair-programming for coding blocks, more review/architecture work, and ergonomic equipment.

michael: Pairing 1hr/day and switching to review-heavy tasks sounds good. Also would appreciate a trackball/ergonomic keyboard provided if possible.

jamie: I can move your highest-priority tickets to @alex this week and take care of rotation for the next 6 weeks. Alex — can you pick up urgent pager overlap?

alex: Yep I can handle overlap. DM me the list and I'll triage.

people-ops-bot: Accommodation request received: ACC-2026-112. Please upload supporting docs at `hr.redwood.com/accommodations` to move forward.

anya: Quick note — accommodation adjustments don't automatically pause performance conversations, but we will avoid using medical info as a negative. If you need goals adjusted, we'll propose temporary goal tweaks during the accommodation.

jamie: Understood. I'll adjust quarterly goals and annotate the plan so it's clear which tasks were reallocated.

michael: Thank you. One question on process: how formal is the plan? Will it show up on my HR record?

anya: We'll create an accommodation plan document that lives in HR and is accessible to you and your manager. It's a record of agreed changes and timelines. We keep medical details minimal.

michael: Uploaded the doc and doctor's note just now.

anya: Got it — thanks. I'll draft the accommodation plan and share it for sign-off. I'll also submit an equipment request for the trackball/keyboard under the accommodation budget.

jamie: I'll reassign tickets and adjust the on-call schedule tomorrow. Thanks all.

michael: Really appreciate the quick help. 10am intake call tomorrow works for me.

anya: Great — sending calendar invite for 10:00 AM tomorrow for intake (you + manager). If you'd rather keep it manager-free for the first call, say so and we can do a private intake. :thumbsup:

michael: Manager join is fine. Thanks again.
